# 1.1 TB incidence

_Draft! Prepared `r Sys.Date()` using country-reported data snapshot files from `r snapshot_date` and incidence estimates from `r est_date`_

An estimated global total of `r round(global$inc.num[global$year==yr]/1e6,1)` million people (95% uncertainty interval [UI]: `r round(global$inc.lo.num[global$year==yr]/1e6,1)`–`r round(global$inc.hi.num[global$year==yr]/1e6,1)` million) fell ill with TB in `r yr`, equivalent to `r round(global$inc[global$year==yr],0)` incident cases (95% UI: `r round(global$inc.lo[global$year==yr],0)`–`r round(global$inc.hi[global$year==yr],0)`) per `r cm` population (`r lnk("Table 1.1.1")`). Among all incident TB cases, `r round(100*global$inc.h.num[global$year==yr]/global$inc.num[global$year==yr],1)`% were among people living with HIV. Most TB cases in `r yr` were in the WHO regions of South-East Asia (`r round(100*regional$inc.num[regional$year==yr & regional$g.whoregion=="SEA"]/global$inc.num[global$year==yr],0)`%), the Western Pacific (`r round(100*regional$inc.num[regional$year==yr & regional$g.whoregion=="WPR"]/global$inc.num[global$year==yr],0)`%) and Africa (`r round(100*regional$inc.num[regional$year==yr & regional$g.whoregion=="AFR"]/global$inc.num[global$year==yr],0)`%), with smaller shares in the Eastern Mediterranean (`r round(100*regional$inc.num[regional$year==yr & regional$g.whoregion=="EMR"]/global$inc.num[global$year==yr],1)`%), the Americas (`r round(100*regional$inc.num[regional$year==yr & regional$g.whoregion=="AMR"]/global$inc.num[global$year==yr],1)`%) and Europe (`r round(100*regional$inc.num[regional$year==yr & regional$g.whoregion=="EUR"]/global$inc.num[global$year==yr],1)`%).

In `r yr`, the estimated number of people who fell ill with TB worldwide decreased for the second consecutive year, continuing the reversal of increases between 2020 and 2023 that occurred during and in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic (`r lnk("Fig. 1.1.1")`, panel a). The TB incidence rate (new cases per `r cm` population per year) also continued to decrease, by `r round(100-(100*global$inc[global$year==yr]/global$inc[global$year==yr-1]),1)`% between 2024 and 2025 (`r lnk("Fig. 1.1.1")`, panel b), and is now below the level of 2020 (the historic low, pre-COVID).

Globally, the net reduction in the TB incidence rate from 2015 to `r yr` was `r ftb(100-(100*global$inc[global$year==yr]/global$inc[global$year==2015]))`%, far short of the WHO End TB Strategy milestone of a `r (1-inc.milestone.vs.2015)*100`% reduction by `r inc.mort.milestone.yr` (`r ref_lnk("1, 2")`).

### `r anch("Fig. 1.1.1")`<span class="red">Fig. 1.1.1</span> Global trends in the estimated number of incident TB cases (a) and the incidence rate (b), 2010&#8211;`r yr`
<div class="subhead">Shaded areas represent 95% uncertainty intervals. The horizontal dashed line shows the `r inc.mort.milestone.yr` milestone of the End TB Strategy, which was a `r (1-inc.milestone.vs.2015)*100`% reduction in the TB incidence rate between 2015 and `r inc.mort.milestone.yr`.</div>


<hr />
<br />

The estimated increases in TB incidence between 2020 and 2023 were the consequence of disruptions to TB diagnosis and treatment during the COVID-19 pandemic, when the reported number of people newly diagnosed with TB fell from `r round(global$c.newinc[global$year==2019]/1e6,1)` million in 2019 to `r round(global$c.newinc[global$year==2020]/1e6,1)` million in 2020 and `r round(global$c.newinc[global$year==2021]/1e6,1)` million in 2021 (`r lnk("Fig. 1.1.1")`; <span class="red">Section 2.1</span>). These reductions were assumed to have resulted in an increase in the number of people with untreated TB and an associated increase in transmission.

The big global recovery in the reported number of people newly diagnosed with TB in 2022 and 2023, which was then consolidated in 2024 and 2025 (<span class="red">Section 2.1</span>), has resulted in first a slowing of increases in TB incidence, and then a reversal of the upward trend. In `r yr`, both the TB incidence rate and the estimated number of people who fell ill with TB continued to decrease, for the second consecutive year since the COVID-19 pandemic.

In `r yr`, `r f1.1.2_top |> nrow() |> int2word()` countries accounted for about two thirds of global TB cases: `r f1.1.2_top[1,"country.in.text.EN"]` (`r ftb(f1.1.2_top[1,"pct"])`%), `r f1.1.2_top[2,"country.in.text.EN"]` (`r ftb(f1.1.2_top[2,"pct"])`%), `r f1.1.2_top[3,"country.in.text.EN"]` (`r ftb(f1.1.2_top[3,"pct"])`%), `r f1.1.2_top[4,"country.in.text.EN"]` (`r ftb(f1.1.2_top[4,"pct"])`%), `r f1.1.2_top[5,"country.in.text.EN"]` (`r ftb(f1.1.2_top[5,"pct"])`%), `r f1.1.2_top[6,"country.in.text.EN"]` (`r ftb(f1.1.2_top[6,"pct"])`%), `r f1.1.2_top[7,"country.in.text.EN"]` (`r ftb(f1.1.2_top[7,"pct"])`%) and `r f1.1.2_top[8,"country.in.text.EN"]` (`r ftb(f1.1.2_top[8,"pct"])`%) (`r lnk("Fig. 1.1.2")` and `r lnk("Fig. 1.1.3")`).

### `r anch("Fig. 1.1.3")`<span class="red">Fig. 1.1.3</span> Geographic distribution of the estimated global number of incident TB cases in `r yr`

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results = "asis", dev = 'png', fig_1.1.3, fig.alt="Share of the number of incident TB cases in 2025"} 


library(treemapify)

plot_data113 <- est %>%
  select(iso3,country,year,g.whoregion,inc.num) %>%
  subset(year==yr) %>%
  arrange(desc(inc.num)) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
  mutate(label_text = ifelse(rank <= 10, country, ""))

custom_region_labels <- c(
  "AFR" = "African Region",
  "AMR" = "Region of the Americas",
  "EMR" = "Eastern Mediterranean Region",
  "EUR" = "European Region", 
  "SEA" = "South-East Asia Region",
  "WPR" = "Western Pacific Region"
)

f1.1.3_plot <- ggplot(plot_data113, aes(area = inc.num, fill = g.whoregion, label = label_text)) +
  # Draw the rectangles representing burden size
  geom_treemap(show.legend = TRUE, color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  # Add the text labels using our custom column
  geom_treemap_text(
    colour = "white", # White text contrasts well with colorful fills
    place = "centre", # Center the labels
    grow = FALSE,     # Set to TRUE if you want labels to fill the box size
    reflow = TRUE     # Wrap long country names onto multiple lines
  ) +
  # Add titles and theme
  labs(
    fill = "WHO region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3",
                    labels = custom_region_labels)

output_ggplot(f1.1.3_plot, plot_data113, show_static=TRUE, pdf_csv_folder, save_csv, save_pdf)

```
<!-- <div class="footnote">Estimates of TB incidence for India are <strong>interim</strong>. See <span style="color: red;">Annex 4</span> of the core report document.</div> -->

<hr />
<br />

The severity of national TB epidemics, in terms of the number of incident TB cases per `r cm` population in `r yr`, varies widely among countries: from less than 10 to more than 500 cases per `r cm` population  (`r lnk("Fig. 1.1.4")`). 

In `r yr`, countries with the highest rates were mostly in the WHO African Region, where `r count(est,year==yr & inc>=300 & g.whoregion=="AFR")[[2,2]]` countries had a rate of more than 300 per `r cm` population. There were `r count(est,year==yr & inc<10 & g.whostatus=="M")[[2,2]]` countries with a low incidence of TB (<10 cases per `r cm` population), mostly in the WHO Region of the Americas and the European Region, plus a few countries in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean and Western Pacific regions.

```{r}
year_with_highest_tbhiv <- global$year[which.max(global$tbhiv)]
```


In `r yr`, the global proportion of people with a new episode of TB (either new or recurrent cases) who were living with HIV was `r round(100*global$tbhiv[global$year==yr],1)`% (95% UI: `r round(100*global$tbhiv.lo[global$year==yr],1)`&#8211;`r round(100*global$tbhiv.hi[global$year==yr],1)`%) and was highest in countries in the WHO African Region, exceeding 50% in parts of southern Africa (`r lnk("Fig. 1.1.5")`). The proportion has been falling for many years, following a peak at `r round(100*global$tbhiv[global$year==year_with_highest_tbhiv],0)`% in `r year_with_highest_tbhiv`.

<hr /> 
<br />

TB can affect anyone, regardless of age or sex (`r lnk("Fig. 1.1.6")`). The highest burden is in adult men (aged &#8805;15 years), with an estimated  `r round(inc.men/1e6,1)` million cases (95% UI: `r round(inc.men.lo/1e6,1)`–`r round(inc.men.hi/1e6,1)` million) in `r yr`, equivalent to  `r round(100*inc.men/global$inc.num[global$year==yr],0)`% of the estimated total; by comparison, there were an estimated `r round(inc.women/1e6,1)` million cases (95% UI: `r round(inc.women.lo/1e6,1)`–`r round(inc.women.hi/1e6,1)` million) among adult women (aged &#8805;15 years), equivalent to `r round(100*inc.women/global$inc.num[global$year==yr],0)`% of the estimated total, and `r round(inc.child/1e6,1)` million (95% UI: `r round(inc.child.lo/1e6,2)`–`r round(inc.child.hi/1e6,1)` million) cases among children and young adolescents (aged 0–14 years), equivalent to `r round(100*inc.child/global$inc.num[global$year==yr],0)`% of the estimated total. 

Case notifications of people newly diagnosed with TB in `r yr` were `r round(100*global$c.newinc[global$year==yr]/global$inc.num[global$year==yr],0)`% of the estimated TB incidence overall, with the same figures for adult men and women (`r round(100*sum(globsplt$newrel[globsplt$sex=="M"& globsplt$age %ni% c("0-4","5-14") ])/sum(globsplt$inc[globsplt$sex=="M"& globsplt$age %ni% c("0-4","5-14")]),0)`%). The figure was much lower for children and young adolescents aged 0–14 years (`r round(100*sum(globsplt$newrel[globsplt$age %in% c("0-4","5-14")])/sum(globsplt$inc[globsplt$age %in% c("0-4","5-14")]),0)`%) and lower still for children aged <5 years (`r round(100*sum(globsplt$newrel[globsplt$age=="0-4"])/sum(globsplt$inc[globsplt$age=="0-4"]),0)`%). 

Global estimates of TB incidence during pregnancy and postpartum, in 2023 specifically, have been published recently (`r ref_lnk("3")`). It was estimated that `r formatC(239500, format="f", big.mark=" ", digits=0)` pregnant women (95% UI `r formatC(216300, format="f", big.mark=" ", digits=0)`–`r formatC(262800, format="f", big.mark=" ", digits=0)`) and `r formatC(97600, format="f", big.mark=" ", digits=0)` postpartum women (95% UI `r formatC(90100, format="f", big.mark=" ", digits=0)`–`r formatC(105200, format="f", big.mark=" ", digits=0)`) developed TB globally in 2023.

Regional estimates of the distribution of incident TB cases, disaggregated by age and sex and compared with case notifications, are shown in `r lnk("Fig. 1.1.7")`. The largest numbers are typically in the age groups of 25–34, 35–44 or 45–54 years. The WHO Western Pacific Region is an exception, with the largest number of cases in the age group &#8805;65 years; this is mostly influenced by numbers for China and can be explained by the country’s aging population and declining burden of TB disease (with higher rates of infection and a higher risk of new cases arising from reactivation of previous infections among older people).

### `r anch("Fig. 1.1.8")`<span class="red">Fig. 1.1.8</span> Trends in estimated TB incidence rates by WHO region, 2010&#8211;`r yr`
<div class="subhead">The overall TB incidence rate is shown in <span style="color:#91A93E">green</span> and the incidence rate among people living with HIV is shown in <span style="color:#ED1D24">red</span>. The black solid lines show case notifications of people newly diagnosed with TB, for comparison with estimates of the overall incidence rate. Shaded areas represent 95% uncertainty intervals. The horizontal dashed line shows the `r inc.mort.milestone.yr` milestone of the End TB Strategy, which was a `r (1-inc.milestone.vs.2015)*100`% reduction in the TB incidence rate between 2015 and `r inc.mort.milestone.yr`.  </div> 
```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results = "asis", dev = 'png', fig.height=8,  fig_1.1.8, fig.alt="Trends in estimated TB incidence rates by WHO region, 2000-2025"} 

f1.1.8_plot <- qplot(year,
      inc,
      data = subset(regional,year>=2010),
      geom = 'line',
      colour = I('blue')) +
  geom_line(aes(year, inc.h), colour = I('lightskyblue2')) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(year, ymin = inc.h.lo, ymax = inc.h.hi),
              fill = I('lightskyblue2'),
              alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(year, ymin = inc.lo, ymax = inc.hi),
              fill = I('blue'),
              alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(year, newinc)) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = inc.milestone), linetype = I(2)) +
  facet_wrap(~ region, scale = 'free_y') +
  xlab('') + ylab('Number per 100 000 population per year') +
  expand_limits(y=1) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  #  scale_y_continuous(trans='log10', breaks=c(1,2,5,10,20,30,50,100,200,300)) +
 # scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(2010,2015,2020,2025)) +
  theme_gtb() +
  theme(legend.position = 'none') 

output_ggplot(f1.1.8_plot, subset(regional,year>=2010), show_static, pdf_csv_folder, save_csv, save_pdf)


```

<hr />
<br />




In `r yr`, the TB incidence rate increased for the fifth consecutive year in the WHO Region of the Americas, reflecting the estimated impact of shortfalls in TB case detection in 2020 and a still incomplete recovery by `r yr`. In the Western Pacific Region, the TB incidence rate has been declining since 2024, following an upward trend in 2020–2023. In 2 other WHO regions, the Eastern Mediterranean Region and the South-East Asia Region, the TB incidence rate decreased for a third consecutive year, continuing to reinforce the 2023 reversal of the 2020–2022 COVID-related upward trend. In the WHO European Region, the TB incidence rate has been falling since 2021. In the WHO African Region, the decline in the TB incidence rate that has been sustained for many years (including during the COVID-19 pandemic) continued in `r yr`.

The biggest estimated reduction in the TB incidence rate since the End TB Strategy baseline year of 2015 has been in the WHO European Region, with a net reduction of `r round(100-100*regional$inc[regional$year==yr & regional$g.whoregion=="EUR"]/regional$inc[regional$year==2015 & regional$g.whoregion=="EUR"],0)`% by `r yr`. This was mainly driven by progress in the Russian Federation. A large reduction has also been achieved in the African Region, with a `r round(100-100*regional$inc[regional$year==yr & regional$g.whoregion=="AFR"]/regional$inc[regional$year==2015 & regional$g.whoregion=="AFR"],0)`% decline by `r yr`. In the South-East Asia Region, the decline was `r round(100-100*regional$inc[regional$year==yr & regional$g.whoregion=="SEA"]/regional$inc[regional$year==2015 & regional$g.whoregion=="SEA"],0)`%. The net decline in `r yr` compared with 2015 was relatively small in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (`r round(100-100*regional$inc[regional$year==yr & regional$g.whoregion=="EMR"]/regional$inc[regional$year==2015 & regional$g.whoregion=="EMR"],1)`%). 

There was no net decline in the Western Pacific Region, due to increases in Indonesia, the Philippines and Papua New Guinea that cancelled out reductions in other countries. Between 2015 and `r yr`, there was a net increase in TB incidence in one WHO region: the Region of the Americas (up `r round(100*regional$inc[regional$year==yr & regional$g.whoregion=="AMR"]/regional$inc[regional$year==2015 & regional$g.whoregion=="AMR"]-100,0)`%).

Regional trends in the estimated number of people who fell ill with TB are available in <span class="red">Figure 2.3.1</span> (<span class="red">Section 2.3</span>). 


Trends in TB incidence rates by income group are shown in `r lnk("Fig. 1.1.9")`.

```{r}
dta <- subset(est, year==yr, select=c("iso3","country","year","inc"))
dta_2015 <- subset(est, year==2015, select=c("iso3","inc"))
setnames(dta_2015, "inc", "inc.2015")
dta <- merge(dta, dta_2015, by="iso3")
rm(dta_2015)

dta$rel.red.inc=(1-(dta$inc/dta$inc.2015))*100
dta$rel.red.inc.cat=ifelse(dta$rel.red.inc>0,"Reduction","Increase")

dta$rel.red.inc.fordisplay=ifelse(dta$rel.red.inc<0,
                                      -round(dta$rel.red.inc,1),
                                      round(dta$rel.red.inc,1))

dta$var <- cut(
  dta$rel.red.inc,
  c(-Inf,-5,5, 10, 20, 50,Inf),
  c("Increase (>5%)",'Stable (-5% to +5%)', 'Decrease (6\u20139%)', 'Decrease (10\u201319%)', 'Decrease (20\u201349%)','Decrease (\u226550%)'),
  right = F,
  ordered_result = T
)

dta[iso3=="PRK", var:=NA]

dta=merge(dta,cty[,.(iso3,g.whostatus,g.whoregion)],by="iso3")
reach.milestone.lst=dta[var=="Decrease (≥50%)" & g.whostatus=="M",unique(iso3)]
n.reach.milestone=length(reach.milestone.lst)

reach.20pct=dta[(var=="Decrease (≥50%)" | var=="Decrease (20–49%)") & g.whostatus=="M",unique(iso3)]
n.reach.20pct=length(reach.20pct)


reach.20pct.afreur=dta[(var=="Decrease (≥50%)" | var=="Decrease (20–49%)") & g.whostatus=="M" & (g.whoregion=="AFR" | g.whoregion=="EUR"),unique(iso3)]
n.reach.20pct.afreur=length(reach.20pct.afreur)

incr.5pct=dta[var=="Increase (>5%)" & g.whostatus=="M",unique(iso3)]
n.incr.5pct=length(incr.5pct)


```



Progress in reducing the TB incidence rate at country level is highly variable (`r lnk("Fig. 1.1.10")`). In total, `r n.reach.20pct` countries (including `r n.reach.20pct.afreur` in the WHO European and African regions) achieved estimated reductions of at least 20% between 2015 and `r yr`, thus reaching or surpassing the first (2020) milestone of the End TB Strategy; and `r n.reach.milestone` countries are estimated to have achieved reductions of at least 50% between 2015 and `r yr`, including 2 high TB burden countries (Namibia and South Africa). At the other extreme, there are `r n.incr.5pct` countries where the TB incidence rate in `r yr` was more than 5% higher than in 2015. These countries are most noticeably in the WHO Region of the Americas but also include three high TB burden countries in Asia: Indonesia, Myanmar and the Philippines.

The horizontal dashed line shows the `r inc.mort.milestone.yr` milestone of the End TB Strategy, which was a `r (1-inc.milestone.vs.2015)*100`% reduction between 2015 and `r inc.mort.milestone.yr`.</div>

`r lnk("Box 1.1.1")` provides a summary of the methods used to produce estimates of TB incidence for the period 2010–`r yr`. 

`r anch("Box 1.1.1")`



```{r}

load(here("inc_mort/analysis/est.method.rda"))

est.meth.inc=est.method[,.(iso3,method.inc)]

est.meth.inc= est.meth.inc %>% 
  mutate(
  var=case_when(
  method.inc>=1 & method.inc<=3 ~ "Case notifications and UHC SCI",
  method.inc>=4 & method.inc<=6 ~ "Case notifications and UHC SCI with statistical model",
  method.inc>=7 & method.inc<=9 ~ "National TB prevalence survey",
  method.inc>=10 & method.inc<=12 ~ "National TB inventory study",
  method.inc==13 ~ "National TB prevalence survey combined with VR data",  
  method.inc==991 ~ "Case notifications combined with TB mortality data",
  method.inc==992 ~ "Country-specific customized approach",
  method.inc==993 ~ "Case notifications with no adjustment (<10 episodes of TB)",
  method.inc==994 ~ "Case notifications with no adjustment",
  method.inc==995 ~ "Case notifications with standard adjustment",
)
)

country_counts <- est.meth.inc %>%
  group_by(var) %>%
  summarise(n_countries = n_distinct(iso3)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_countries))



cm.lst <- union(unique(est.meth.inc$iso3[est.meth.inc$method.inc %in% c(2, 5, 8, 11)]),"BRA")
rm.lst <- unique(est.meth.inc$iso3[est.meth.inc$method.inc %in% c(3, 6, 9, 12)])

country_names <- cty %>%
  filter(iso3 %in% cm.lst) %>%
  pull(country) %>%
  sub("^Philippines$", "the Philippines", .)

country_model_list <- paste0(
  paste(country_names[-length(country_names)], collapse = ", "),
  " and ",
  country_names[length(country_names)]
)




# Share in 2024

inc_iso3 <- est[year==yr,.(iso3,inc.num)]
inc_tot=global$inc.num[global$year==yr]

category_data <- inc_iso3 %>%
  left_join(est.meth.inc %>% select(iso3, var), by = "iso3")


category_shares <- category_data %>%
  group_by(var) %>%
  summarise(
    n_countries = n_distinct(iso3),
    cat_inc = sum(inc.num, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    share_pct = (cat_inc / inc_tot) * 100,
    Formatted_Share = case_when(
      share_pct >= 10 ~ paste0(round(share_pct, 0), "%"),
      share_pct < 0.1 ~ "<0.1%",
      TRUE ~ paste0(round(share_pct, 1), "%")
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(share_pct))







library(treemap)
library(treemapify)

light_palette <- c(
  "#8dd3c7", "#ffffb3", "#bebada", "#fb8072", "#80b1d3", 
  "#fdb462", "#b3de69", "#fccde5", "#bc80bd", "#ccebc5"
)

df_treemap <- category_shares %>% 
  mutate(
    formatted_share = ifelse(share_pct >= 10, round(share_pct, 0), round(share_pct, 1)),
    label_text = paste0(n_countries, " countries\n(", formatted_share, "%)"),
    var = reorder(var, -share_pct)
  )

treemap_method <- ggplot(df_treemap, aes(area = cat_inc, fill = var, label = label_text)) +
  geom_treemap() +
  geom_treemap_text(
    colour = "black", 
    place = "centre", 
    grow = FALSE, 
    size = 9,           # Slightly adjusted base size to fit more boxes
    min.size = 1        # Forces text to appear even on very small tiles (default is usually 4)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = light_palette) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    fill = "Estimation Method"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2, override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "vertical",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold")
  )

share.cm=round(100*sum(inc_iso3$inc.num[inc_iso3$iso3 %in% cm.lst],na.rm=T)/inc_tot,0)
share.rm=round(100*sum(inc_iso3$inc.num[inc_iso3$iso3 %in% rm.lst],na.rm=T)/inc_tot,1)


```



<div class="textbox">
## Box 1.1.1 

## Methods used by WHO to estimate TB incidence 


The main methods used by WHO to estimate TB incidence at country level in the period 2010–`r yr` are shown in `r lnk("Fig. 1.1.13")`; additional details are provided in `r lnk("Table 1.1.2")`. These methods adhere to global guidelines for accurate and transparent reporting of health estimates (`r ref_lnk("4")`) and are described in detail in a <span class="red">technical appendix</span>. 

Updates to methods used for this report are explained in <span class="red">Annex 4</span> of the core report document. The main update for this report is the use of a new approach to estimate TB incidence in Mongolia and Thailand, using a combination of TB mortality data from a national vital registration system, TB case notification data and results from national TB prevalence surveys.

In addition, updates to estimates based on values of the Universal Health Coverage Service Coverage Index (UHC SCI) and TB case notification data were made for `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications and UHC SCI with statistical model") %>% pull(n_countries)+category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications and UHC SCI") %>% pull(n_countries)` countries, using the latest time series of UHC SCI estimates; these were previously available for 2000–2021 but have now been extended to cover the period 2000–2023. 




<!-- ### `r anch("Fig. 1.1.13")`<span class="red">Fig. 1.1.13</span> Main methods used to estimate TB incidence, 2010&#8211;`r yr`  -->

<!-- ```{r echo=FALSE, fig.height=6.5 , message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results = "asis", dev = 'png', fig_1.1.13a, fig.alt="Main methods used to estimate TB incidence, 2010–2025"}  -->

<!-- treemap_method -->
<!-- ``` -->

<hr />
<br />

<!-- Methods used by WHO to estimate TB incidence for 2010–`r yr` included: -->

<!-- * Results from national TB prevalence surveys combined with estimates of the duration of disease, used for `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "National TB prevalence survey") %>% pull(n_countries)` countries with `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "National TB prevalence survey") %>% pull(Formatted_Share)` of the global number of incident TB cases in `r yr`; This includes India where a country-specific dynamic model that was calibrated to survey data as well as other data (e.g. notifications, drug sales) and WHO TB mortality estimates was used (for further details, see the <span class="red">technical appendix</span>). -->

<!-- * Results from national TB prevalence surveys combined data from the vital registration system and TB case notifications was used in `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "National TB prevalence survey combined with VR data") %>% pull(n_countries)` with `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "National TB prevalence survey combined with VR data") %>% pull(Formatted_Share)` of the global number of incident TB cases in `r yr`; -->

<!-- <!-- * Results from a national TB prevalence survey combined with a country-specific dynamic model that was calibrated to survey data as well as other data (e.g. notifications, drug sales) and WHO TB mortality estimates. This was used for India, which had `r  `% of the global number of incident TB cases in `r yr` (for further details, see the <span class="red">technical appendix</span>); --> 

<!-- * Results from national inventory studies that measured the level of underreporting of detected TB cases, used for `r  category_shares %>% filter(var == "National TB inventory study") %>% pull(n_countries)` countries with about `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "National TB inventory study") %>% pull(Formatted_Share)` of the global number of incident TB cases in `r yr`; -->

<!-- * TB notifications upward adjusted according to an incidence:notification ratio derived from a UHC SCI-based statistical model, used for `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications and UHC SCI with statistical model") %>% pull(n_countries)` countries with `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications and UHC SCI with statistical model") %>% pull(Formatted_Share)` of the global number of incident TB cases in `r yr`; -->

<!-- * TB notifications upward adjusted according to country-specific values for the UHC SCI, used for `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications and UHC SCI") %>% pull(n_countries)` countries with `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications and UHC SCI") %>% pull(Formatted_Share)` of the global number of incident TB cases in `r yr`; -->

<!-- * A country-specific customized approach, which was used for `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Country-specific customized approach") %>% pull(n_countries)` African countries for which the UHC SCI methods did not work well. These countries accounted for `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Country-specific customized approach") %>% pull(Formatted_Share)` of the global number of incident TB cases in `r yr`; -->

<!-- * TB notifications combined with TB mortality data from a national vital registration system. This was used for Brazil, which had `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications combined with TB mortality data") %>% pull(Formatted_Share)`  of the global number of incident TB cases in `r yr`; -->

<!-- * TB notifications with no adjustment, used for `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications with no adjustment (<10 episodes of TB)") %>% pull(n_countries)` countries that reported less than 10 cases of TB in `r  ` and `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications with no adjustment") %>% pull(n_countries)` countries for which country-specific evidence suggested that no adjustment was appropriate (e.g. due to high levels of population-based screening as well as potential for overdiagnosis), which accounted for respectively `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications with no adjustment (<10 episodes of TB)") %>% pull(Formatted_Share)` and `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications with no adjustment") %>% pull(Formatted_Share)` of the global number of incident cases in `r yr`; -->

<!-- * TB notifications and a standard upward adjustment to account for underreporting, overdiagnosis and underdiagnosis, retained based on bilateral discussions with national TB programmes for `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications with standard adjustment") %>% pull(n_countries)` countries for which this method had previously been used for several years, which accounted for about `r category_shares %>% filter(var == "Case notifications with standard adjustment") %>% pull(Formatted_Share)` of the global number of incident TB cases in `r yr` -->



### `r anch("Fig. 1.1.13")`<span class="red">Fig. 1.1.13</span> Main methods used to estimate TB incidence, 2010&#8211;`r yr` 
<div class="subhead"> A country-specific dynamic model has been used in `r country_model_list` to account for COVID-19 disruptions. </div> 


```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results = "asis", dev = 'png', fig_1.1.13, fig.alt="Main methods used to estimate TB incidence, 2010–2025"} 


ordered_methods <- category_shares %>%
  arrange(desc(share_pct)) %>%
  pull(var)

method1 <- est.meth.inc %>%
  select(iso3, var) %>%
  mutate(var = factor(var, levels = ordered_methods))

method1[iso3=="PRK", var:=NA]


f1.1.13_plot <- whomapper(
  X = method1, water_col = 'white',
  legend_title = 'Estimation method',
  colours = light_palette,
  legend_pos = c(0.12,0.48)
  )


output_ggplot(f1.1.13_plot, dta, show_static=TRUE, pdf_csv_folder, save_csv, save_pdf)

```

### `r anch("Table 1.1.2")`<span class="red">Table 1.1.2</span> Main methods used to estimate TB incidence, 2010&#8211;`r yr` 


```{r tab_1.1.2}

table_data <- category_shares %>% 
  mutate(
    Formatted_Share = case_when(
      share_pct >= 10 ~ paste0(round(share_pct, 0), "%"),
      share_pct < 0.1 ~ "<0.1%",
      TRUE ~ paste0(round(share_pct, 1), "%")
    ),
    var = as.character(var)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(share_pct)) %>%
  select(
    `Estimation Method` = var,
    `Number of countries` = n_countries,
    `Share of total TB incidence` = Formatted_Share
  )


table_data_full <- table_data %>%
  mutate(
    Description = case_when(
      `Estimation Method` == "National TB prevalence survey" ~ "Results from national TB prevalence surveys combined with estimates of the duration of disease; this includes India where a country-specific dynamic model that was calibrated to survey data as well as other data (e.g. notifications, drug sales) and WHO TB mortality estimates was used.",
      `Estimation Method` == "National TB inventory study" ~ "Measured level of underreporting of detected TB cases.",
      `Estimation Method` == "Case notifications and UHC SCI with statistical model" ~ "TB notifications upward adjusted according to an incidence:notification ratio derived from a UHC SCI-based statistical model.",
      `Estimation Method` == "Country-specific customized approach" ~ "Customized approach used for countries where UHC SCI methods did not work well.",
      `Estimation Method` == "Case notifications and UHC SCI" ~ "TB notifications upward adjusted according to country-specific values for the UHC SCI.",
      `Estimation Method` == "National TB prevalence survey combined with VR data" ~ "Results from national TB prevalence surveys combined with TB mortality data from a national vital registration system and TB case notifications.",
      `Estimation Method` == "Case notifications combined with TB mortality data" ~ "TB notifications combined with TB mortality data from a national vital registration system (used for Brazil).",
      `Estimation Method` == "Case notifications with no adjustment" ~ "Countries for which country-specific evidence suggested that no adjustment was appropriate (e.g. due to high levels of population-based screening as well as potential for overdiagnosis).",
      `Estimation Method` == "Case notifications with standard adjustment" ~ "TB notifications and a standard upward adjustment to account for underreporting, overdiagnosis and underdiagnosis, used until 2024 and retained for use in 2025 and 2026 based on bilateral discussions with national TB programmes.",
      `Estimation Method` == "Case notifications with no adjustment (<10 episodes of TB)" ~ "TB notifications with no adjustment, used for countries that reported fewer than 10 cases of TB.",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

table_data_full <- table_data_full %>%
  select(
    `Estimation method` = `Estimation Method`,
    Description,
    `Number of countries`,
    `Share of total TB incidence` 
  )



knitr::kable(table_data_full, format = "html", align = 'rrcc', table.attr = "id='method_table'")
```

<hr />
<br />


For `r  length(cm.lst) + length(rm.lst)` countries with the biggest absolute reductions in TB notifications during the COVID-19 pandemic that were a clear departure from historic trends, estimates of TB incidence in 2020–`r yr` were based on country-specific dynamic models: `r country_model_list`. These methods are described in detail in a <span class="red">technical appendix</span>. For all other countries, the same methods as those used for the period 2010–2019 continued to be applied.


</div>


Country-specific details are available in the [Global tuberculosis report app](https://www.who.int/teams/global-tuberculosis-programme/data#app) and [country profiles](https://worldhealthorg.shinyapps.io/tb_profiles/).


Note: All of the percentage reductions or increases referred to in the text of this webpage were calculated based on unrounded numbers, as opposed to the rounded numbers that appear in the interactive graphics.

```{js, echo=FALSE}
function tb_format_thou_2(n) { 
  //return thousands formatted to to significant figures
  nt = n/1000; 
  return num_spacer(Number(nt.toPrecision(2))*1000)
}

/* Functions to create the figures */

function createFig_1_1_1a(fig_ID) {
 
		$(fig_ID).kendoChart({
			dataSource: fig_1_1_1a_data,
			chartArea: {
				height: 500
			},	
			legend: {
				position: "bottom"
			},
      series: [{
				type: "line",
        name: "All TB cases",
				field: "inc_num",
				color: "#91A93E",
				tooltip: {
					visible: true,
					template: "All TB cases (#= category #): #= tb_format_thou(value) # 000"
				}
			},{
				type: "rangeArea",
				fromField: "inc_lo_num",
				toField: "inc_hi_num",
				color: "#91A93E",
				tooltip: {
					visible: true,
				format: "{0}",
				template: "95% uncertainty interval (#= category #): #= tb_format_thou(value.from) # 000–#= tb_format_thou(value.to) # 000"
				}
			},{
				type: "line",
        name: "Notifications of new and recurrent cases",
				field: "c_newinc",
				color: "black",
				tooltip: {
					visible: true,
					format: "{0}",
					template: "Notifications of new and recurrent cases (#= category #): #= num_spacer(value) #"
				}
			},{
				type: "line",
        name: "TB cases in people living with HIV",
				field: "inc_h_num",
				color: "#ED1D24",
				tooltip: {
					visible: true,
					template: "TB cases in people living with HIV (#= category #): #= tb_format_thou(value) # 000"
				}
			},{
				type: "rangeArea",
				fromField: "inc_h_lo_num",
				toField: "inc_h_hi_num",
				color: "#ED1D24",
				tooltip: {
					visible: true,
				format: "{0}",
				template: "95% uncertainty interval (#= category #): #= tb_format_thou(value.from) # 000–#= tb_format_thou(value.to) # 000"
				}
			},],      
			valueAxis: {

        labels: {
					template: "#= axis_spacer(value/1e6) #"
				},
				title: {
					text: "Millions per year",
					visible: true
				},
        min: 0,

				line: {
					visible: false
				}
			}
			,
			categoryAxis: {
				field: "year",
				labels: {
					rotation: "auto",
          step: 3
				},
				majorGridLines: {
					visible: false
				},
				title: {
					text: "Year",
					visible: true
				}
			}

		});
}



function createFig_1_1_1b(fig_ID) {

			},

			},
      series: [{

				}
			},{
				type: "rangeArea",
				fromField: "inc_lo",
				toField: "inc_hi",
				color: "#91A93E",
				tooltip: {
					visible: true,
				format: "{0}",
				template: "95% uncertainty interval (#= category #): #= num_spacer(value.from) #–#= num_spacer(value.to) #"
				}
			},{
				type: "line",
        name: "Notifications of new and recurrent cases",
				field: "newinc",
				color: "black",
				tooltip: {
					visible: true,
					format: "{0}",
					template: "Notifications of new and recurrent cases (#= category #): #= num_spacer(value) #"
				}
			},{
				type: "line",
        name: "TB cases in people living with HIV",
				field: "inc_h",
				color: "#ED1D24",
				tooltip: {
					visible: true,
					template: "Incidence rate of TB in people living with HIV (#= category #): #= num_spacer(value) #"
				}
			},{
				type: "rangeArea",
				fromField: "inc_h_lo",
				toField: "inc_h_hi",
				color: "#ED1D24",
				tooltip: {
					visible: true,
				format: "{0}",
				template: "95% uncertainty interval (#= category #): #= num_spacer(value.from) #–#= num_spacer(value.to) #"
				}
			},{
        type: "line",
        dashType: "dash",
        field: "inc_milestone",
        color: "grey",
        markers: {
             size: 0,
             opacity: 0
           },
			tooltip: {
				visible: false,
			}
      },],      
      
			valueAxis: {
        labels: {
					template: "#= axis_spacer(value) #"
				},
				title: {
					text: "Number per 100 000 population per year",
					visible: true
				},
        min: 0,
        max: 250,
				line: {
					visible: false
				}
			},      
      render: function (e) {
            var draw = kendo.drawing;
            var padding = 100;
            var padding2 = 300;
            var element = this.element;
            var rect = new kendo.geometry.Rect([padding, padding2], [element.width() - 2 * padding, element.height() - 2 * padding2]);

            var text = new draw.Text("2025 milestone", [0, 0], { font: "bold 9px Verdana,Arial,sans-serif" });
            draw.align([text], rect, "start");
            draw.vAlign([text], rect, "start");
            e.sender.surface.draw(text);
          },
			categoryAxis: {
				field: "year",
				labels: {
					rotation: "auto",
          step: 3
				},
				majorGridLines: {
					visible: false
				},
				title: {
					text: "Year",
					visible: true
				}
			}

		});
}
```
